note: The Caravan (owner, 2026-10-23): the Train becomes a travelling merchant caravan, size 2, one state (arrived). Two concepts, two candidates each.

caravan-covered.prompt: CAMERA AND STYLE REFERENCE: the first attached panel on grass is a building from this game drawn in the game's camera and in this style; match its camera exactly (the front square to the viewer, no side view, the top seen from above, the grid straight), its painterly rendering and its bright daylight. SUBJECT: the MERCHANT CARAVAN, a travelling trader's wagon that rolls into town, parks for two days and buys the settlement's goods, replacing the game's old train. It must read as 'a shop that travels' at a glance: a wagon AND a market stall at once. FAMILY: vehicle. LOOK: town: clean. No people, no merchant figure: only the wagon, the animals and the goods. CONCEPT A, THE COVERED WAGON: a big covered wagon parked square-on, its barrel-vault canvas hood painted in bold TEAL and BURGUNDY stripes with brass fittings and a brass lantern at each corner, big iron-rimmed wooden wheels. Its near side is folded DOWN into a trading counter under a striped awning: on the counter a brass balance scale, a strongbox, sacks of grain, a crate of apples, a wheel of cheese, bolts of cloth; a tall pole with a burgundy pennant. Two shaggy brown OXEN stand unhitched beside the wagon, one eating from a hay bag, the yoke leaning on the wheel. A dusty patch of ground with wheel ruts under it. The LAST attached image is a layout guide, a patch of the board grid with a tan 2 x 2 square: the wagon, its animals and its goods fill that 2 x 2 square almost to its edges, end to end (the wagon's roof, awning and pennant may rise above it), with a soft contact shadow. Fill the surrounding squares with plain short grass in the same style, no props beyond those named, and draw the faint grid lines as thin tile edges. Do not leave the tan square tan. No letters anywhere, no words on any sign.
